For the littles and those who love 'em

The founder of a subverse should have a higher vote weight in their respective subverse than anyone else (i.e. one vote == 5 points), and when they vote they are not only approving of a given post but also approving / disapproving of the user who made the post. This is recorded on a per-user-per-subverse basis as "merit".

As a user's merit grows in a given sub, their votes also become more weighted, and their merit points rub off on those they upvote / downvote.

This system would replace a traditional moderation system: moderators aren't explicitly chosen by the founder but instead their role emerges organically as they gain merit. They are not authorised to delete posts or ban users but instead, their weighted vote gives them a greater say in what content gets buried or featured, and thus the sub moderates itself, gradually morphing into the founder's original vision with minimal effort from those at the helm.

Edit: thought I'd provide some background as to where this idea came from. The subreddit /r/gaybros was originally intended as a place for non-queer, masculine dare I say "normal" homosexual men to congregate to discuss the normal kinds topics men usually discuss; cars, guns, working out, brotherhood. As you can imagine, when the SJWsphere got wind of this, they did everything they could to destroy the subreddit, from biased, hostile interviews to invading and brigading. It was decreed that a positive masculine male identity was not something homosexual males were permitted to have. The founders ended up backing down and letting the sub become the what it is today; a cuddle-pile, indistinguishable from any other "gay" space on the internet, where every other thread is about pride parades and anal hygiene.

I thought about ways that small subs with unpopular opinions like /r/gaybros might be allowed to retain their original culture, and it seemed to me that a meritocracy and weighted vote system, where merit is defined by the founders, would help achieve this.

Naysayers, I would ask that if you disagree with this system, how else could small, controversial subverses protect themselves from tyranny of the majority, without painstaking moderation and cultivation?
